docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This script uses the pyvisa library to communicate with external hardware over VISA protocol (e.g., GPIB, USB, RS232). It’s used to query device identity and test connectivity.

docs.title: This script sets up a Data Acquisition (DAQ) task using NI-DAQmx in
It defines which channels to use, the timing of the acquisition,
and how the DAQ system starts and stops.
docs.text:
Setup python Copy Edit import nidaqmx Import the NI-DAQmx Python library.

python Copy Edit task = nidaqmx.Task() Create a new task object which will manage all DAQ operations.

Channel Configuration python Copy Edit task.ai_channels.add_ai_voltage_chan("Dev1/ai0", min_val=-10.0, max_val=10.0) Add a voltage input channel (AI0) on device Dev1 with a ±10V input range.

Clock and Sampling Rate python Copy Edit task.timing.cfg_samp_clk_timing( * rate=1000, * sample_mode=nidaqmx.constants.AcquisitionType.CONTINUOUS ) Configure the task for continuous acquisition at 1000 samples per second.

Task Execution python Copy Edit task.start() Start the data acquisition task. The DAQ device begins collecting data.

python Copy Edit

docs.title: For example: read data from the buffer, process it, or log it to a file.
docs.text:
python Copy Edit task.stop() Stop the task after acquisition is complete.

python Copy Edit task.close() Close and release the task to free system resources.

Output Summary python Copy Edit

docs.title: - AI0 channel on Dev1 is configured for ±10V analog input.
- Sampling is set to continuous mode at 1 kHz (1000 samples/sec).
- Ready to be used in a loop, logger, or real-time application.
